name: 60/40 stock and bond portfolio

origin.authors: Industry convention; mean-variance theory from Markowitz
origin.source_title: Portfolio Selection (Markowitz 1952) as the theory; the 60/40 split itself has no single paper

how_it_works.simple: Put 60 dollars of every 100 in stocks and 40 in government bonds, and reset to that mix now and then.
how_it_works.analogy: Like a meal that is mostly main course with a big side salad; when one part grows too big you move some back.
how_it_works.precise: A static strategic allocation of 60% equities and 40% intermediate or long government bonds, rebalanced on a calendar schedule. Bonds historically had low or negative correlation with stocks, lowering volatility and drawdown at the cost of some return. It is the standard balanced benchmark for multi-asset strategies.

rule: At each month end (or year end), set weights to 60% S&P 500 total return and 40% 10-year US Treasury total return; hold until the next rebalance.
data_needed: 10-year US Treasury total return or yield series, monthly
economic_rationale: Combining two assets with imperfect correlation lowers risk per unit of return (Markowitz 1952); in the Damodaran annual data a 60/40 mix had a slightly higher Sharpe ratio than stocks alone over 1928 to 2025.
why_it_might_fail: When stocks and bonds fall together the cushion disappears: in 2022 the S&P 500 returned -18.0% and the 10-year Treasury -17.8% per Damodaran, so a 60/40 mix lost about 18%.

reported_results.source: Hurst, Ooi and Pedersen, A Century of Evidence on Trend-Following Investing (AQR)
reported_results.notes: Exhibit 4 of the AQR white paper. The paper notes that no fees or transaction costs are subtracted from the 60/40 portfolio.

reported_results.source: Asness, Frazzini and Pedersen (2012), Leverage Aversion and Risk Parity, Table 2
reported_results.notes: Return is annual excess return over T-bills, rebalanced monthly.

reported_results.source: Our calculation from Damodaran historical returns, 60% S&P 500 and 40% 10-year T-bond
reported_results.notes: Computed by the catalog from the annual table on the page, rebalanced annually. annual_return is geometric; drawdown on annual data understates intra-year drawdown.

reported_results.source: Our calculation from Damodaran historical returns, 60% S&P 500 and 40% 10-year T-bond
reported_results.notes: Computed by the catalog from the annual table on the page, rebalanced annually; geometric annual return.

post_publication_evidence: No publication date to test against. The stock-bond hedge failed in 2022, when the Damodaran data show the S&P 500 at -18.0% and 10-year Treasuries at -17.8%, the worst joint year in the table.

implementations.notes: Has fixed-weight and periodic rebalancing building blocks suited to a 60/40 backtest.

relevance.reason: A common balanced benchmark; useful as a second yardstick next to the S&P 500 when judging a lower-volatility FX strategy.
